paper_title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs

sources.quote: Let a world be a finite set of states z ∈ Z with probabilities p(z) > 0, and let M ≥ 2 modalities observe it, modality m through an injective rendering
sources.rationale: Modelling assumption stipulated by the authors: finite world, each modality an injective rendering of it.

sources.quote: a prediction term ℓ plus an anti-collapse term Ω that depends on f only through the distribution of its embeddings
sources.rationale: Assumed form (1) of the JEPA objective, the same for every modality: encoders into the same R^k, identity predictor, rotation-invariant prediction and anti-collapse terms.

sources.quote: Let M ≥ 2 modalities share one positive-pair distribution
sources.rationale: Hypothesis written in the statement of Theorem 1.

sources.quote: let the minimizers of Lπ be unique up to rotation
sources.rationale: Hypothesis written in the statement of Theorem 1.

sources.quote: one finite world rendered injectively, shared positives, population optima, and minimizers unique up to rotation
sources.rationale: The theorem speaks of exact minimizers of the population objective over all encoders.

sources.quote: each image’s alt-text and two recaptions, written by an image captioner (LLaVA built on LLaMA-3-8B), are its views
sources.rationale: Web alt-texts are collected text; taken alone they carry no pairing information.

sources.quote: two of each image’s three texts are generated by an image captioner (LLaVA built on LLaMA-3-8B, whose vision encoder is CLIP ViT-L/14, 34) and carry information distilled from image–text training
sources.rationale: Texts written from the image by an external pretrained captioner; the paper says they carry information distilled from image-text training.

sources.quote: they require knowing which texts describe the same scene, the grouping of human captions by image on Flickr and COCO
sources.rationale: The labelling that defines good views: which texts belong to the same image. Supplied by design as the definition of positives.

sources.quote: each with the same LeJEPA objective [4] (invariance to the mean of two global views, plus SIGReg with λ = 0.02)
sources.rationale: Engineered training objective of all JEPA runs.

sources.quote: the same BERT made causal, with a tied softmax head
sources.rationale: Engineered training objective of the control arm.

sources.quote: the good-view JEPA reaches .109 on WIT after 21.6M training samples (the texts of 2.16M images)
sources.rationale: Training length chosen for this run; also fixes the data subset (texts of 2.16M images).

sources.quote: We train the 109M-parameter BERT-B text JEPA with 900M samples from the texts of all 940M Recap-DataComp images
sources.rationale: Training length chosen for the large good-view run.

sources.quote: the alignment that next-token prediction reaches after 900M samples (.111, the texts of 940M images; we scored no earlier next-token checkpoint)
sources.rationale: Training length chosen for the next-token run. It is the only checkpoint scored, so it is a set budget, not a measured requirement.

sources.quote: each run uses the recipe of its scale (learning rate 10−4 and batch 256
sources.rationale: Learning rate and batch of the 21.6M-sample good-view run.

sources.quote: and batch 256 against 2 · 10−4 and 2,048)
sources.rationale: Learning rate and batch of the 900M-sample runs; differs from the small-scale recipe.

sources.quote: we pair each text encoder with a frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14
sources.rationale: Pretrained external image encoder used as the vision side.

sources.quote: on the WIT-1024 benchmark of Huh et al. [22], on which none of our models is trained
sources.rationale: Held-out image-caption pairs used to score alignment.

sources.quote: aligned with zero pairs on unpaired halves of COCO train2014
sources.rationale: Images from one half and captions from the other half: collected data with the pairing removed.

sources.quote: since every Flickr image (a world state) has five captions (five nuisances)
sources.rationale: Human captions; which captions share an image is recorded separately in sameImageGrouping.

sources.quote: Data is Flickr30k [70] with the Karpathy split [25]: 29k training images with five captions each
sources.rationale: Photographs used to train the image JEPA.

claims.statement: A good-view text JEPA reaches the same WIT alignment with DINOv2 as next-token prediction on the same corpus with 42 times fewer training samples (21.6M against 900M).
claims.quote: Good views need 42 times fewer training samples than next-token prediction on the same corpus to reach the same alignment

control_usage.quote: the alignment that next-token prediction reaches after 900M samples

claims.notes: Method budget is 21.6M samples; it is left out of method_usage only because the format takes whole numbers. The 900M of the control is its full training length: no earlier next-token checkpoint was scored, and the two runs use different learning rate, batch and data subset.

claims.statement: Theorem 1, together with the applications built on it, makes the Platonic Representation Hypothesis for JEPAs a theorem and a usable tool instead of a hypothesis.
claims.quote: This demonstrates that the PRH– with JEPAs–is no longer a hypothesis but a theorem and a tool.

hypotheses.quote: no experiment meets the hypotheses of Theorem 1 exactly, since our runs use LeJEPA and the image side mostly uses crops as positives
hypotheses.rationale: Section 7 (Known limitations); also Section 2.2 ('in practice the modalities' positives are not the same pairs of world states') and Section 2.3 (the image encoders and DINOv2 use crops of one photograph).

hypotheses.quote: Our theorems are population statements over a finite world with injective renderings and matched marginals; real modalities are lossy
hypotheses.rationale: Section 7 (Known limitations); Section 2.3 adds that a caption sees only part of a photograph, and Section 6 that lossy observations remain open.

hypotheses.quote: When the two embedding dimensions differ (768 for DINOv2, 384 for our text JEPA) we fit a linear map with orthonormal rows, a case the theory does not cover
hypotheses.rationale: Section 2.2, after Proposition 2: the encoders joined in the main experiments and in the captioner have different dimensions (768 or 5,120 against 384), so they cannot be equal up to a rotation in O(k); the paper says the theory does not cover this.

hypotheses.quote: Proposition 1 does not cover uniqueness under its full-distribution constraint, which we leave as an assumption
hypotheses.rationale: Section 2.1 after Proposition 1: proved for whitened second-order anti-collapse with a spectral gap, left as an assumption for the LeJEPA objective the runs use. Openly declared.

hypotheses.quote: finite-sample training relies on the network’s inductive bias
hypotheses.rationale: Section 7: the theorems are population statements; whether trained networks reach these optima is not checked. Openly declared.

hypotheses.quote: As in our experiments, the predictor is the identity
hypotheses.rationale: Section 2.1 and Section A.1: the authors' own JEPA runs use an identity predictor and a rotation-invariant objective (SIGReg in expectation). Recorded for the authors' own JEPA encoders.

claims.notes: Target is the separately trained encoders the paper uses as a tool. For the idealized setting itself the paper states every hypothesis; that reading is claim F3.

claims.statement: Theorem 1: in the idealized model, if all modalities share one positive-pair distribution and the minimizers are unique up to rotation, each modality's minimizer equals one world embedding up to a rotation.
claims.quote: Let M ≥ 2 modalities share one positive-pair distribution, π1 = · · · = π M = π, and let the minimizers of Lπ be unique up to rotation. Then there is one embedding of the world h⋆ : Z → Rk such that every minimizer f m⋆ of Lm , for every modality m, satisfies f m⋆ ◦ gm = Qm h⋆ for some Qm ∈ O(k ), (2) so any two modalities agree up to the single rotation Qm Q⊤ m′ .
claims.notes: Conditional statement. Shared positives and uniqueness are in the statement; finite world, injective renderings, the form of the objective and exact minimizers are in the setup of Section 2.1.

claims.statement: With the same 109M encoder, the same texts and the same 900M training samples, the good-view JEPA aligns with DINOv2 on WIT better than next-token prediction (.184 against .111).
claims.quote: The views make the gain, not the texts. Next-token prediction and the bad-view JEPA trained on the same texts stay far below

method_usage.quote: We train the 109M-parameter BERT-B text JEPA with 900M samples from the texts of all 940M Recap-DataComp images

control_usage.quote: Our three encoders are BERT-B models (109M) trained with 900M samples from the texts of 940M web images

claims.notes: Matched on samples only. A good-view sample reads three texts, the anti-collapse weight of the good-view runs was selected on WIT, and hyperparameters were tuned only for the good-view JEPA.

claims.statement: The rotation between the image encoder and the text JEPA can be found with no image-caption pair, from unpaired images and captions alone.
claims.quote: With no pair at all, the rotation can be found from the geometry of unpaired images and captions
claims.notes: The fit itself uses no pair. The text encoder being aligned was trained on views grouped by image and partly written by an image captioner, which the paper discloses in Sections 7 and C.

claims.statement: The alignment gain of the good-view JEPA on Flickr is due to the objective and not to the information that two captions describe the same image.
claims.quote: the gain comes from the objective and not from the information that two captions describe the same image
claims.notes: Table 1: with the same objective and without the same-image information (bad-view JEPA) the gain mostly disappears. Supported is the weaker reading in the same sentence: the same positives help next-token prediction far less.
